person.name: Tim Hrovat
person.tagline: I build the parts people actually touch

about.body: I care about how software feels to use. It has never been easier to produce something that works, and most of what gets made now stops there, at the first version that runs. What interests me is the version after it: the interaction that lands where you expected, the detail nobody is asked to notice, the code that still reads clearly a year later.
about.craft: That matters more now, not less. Software has never been faster to generate, and generation pulls everything toward the average of what came before. Refinement is the part still left to choose, and people feel it even when they can’t say why.
about.closing: Currently a full stack developer at eŠola, the team behind eAsistent, a school platform used across Slovenia. Alongside it I’m finishing a Computer Science degree at FRI UNI Ljubljana. The thesis is all that’s left.

work.title: Where I’ve worked
work.lead: Six roles over nine years, most of them alongside school and several alongside each other.

easistent.title: Software Developer
description: My first engineering job, and the one that taught me the most. Full stack work on eAsistent, the school platform used by schools, teachers, students and parents across Slovenia. A student contract on paper, but effectively full time for three years, and independent enough to take projects end to end.

highlights.label: Built alone
items: The company UI library. Designed and built on my own, and every new project now starts on it.
The public landing page and the sign-in behind it, end to end.

highlights.label: Across the stack
items: Keeping the legacy code running and integrating with it, then the migrations off it: Laravel 5 to 12, Vue 2 to 3.
The CI/CD pipelines, and the infrastructure they deploy onto.
Backend, frontend and database. The whole path rather than a slice of it.
Prediction models, and the constraint-heavy algorithms behind the timetable generator.

highlights.label: Beyond the code
items: Mentoring new hires and students on placement.
The technical side of our hiring interviews.

easistentLanding.name: eAsistent landing page
easistentLanding.summary: The public face of eAsistent, built end to end, and the sign-in behind it: two-factor, YubiKey, QR-code login from a signed-in phone, PIN and CAPTCHA. That is a lot of ways in, for an audience that ranges from teachers to parents to a fourteen-year-old on a school laptop.

saveTheAnimals.name: Save the Animals
saveTheAnimals.summary: A game written from scratch against SDL2. An exercise in object-oriented design, and in hunting down memory leaks in C++.

wordleEngine.name: Wordle Engine
wordleEngine.summary: A solver that plays Wordle against a dictionary, narrowing the candidate set from each guess. Written in Java with its own test harness to score it over every word in the list.
